caption: The drawing depicts the front view of a two-story building with a classical architectural style, featuring tall cream-colored columns with ornate capitals that support a decorated entablature. The building has multiple rectangular windows with green shutters; the upper and lower floors both have four visible windows. A black wrought-iron fence encloses small patches of grass on either side of a central pathway, which leads to a blue front door under a small portico supported by slender columns. Above the main entrance, there is a second-story balcony with a green metal railing. Red and pink flowering vines or creepers climb and drape over the fence, columns, and balcony, partially obscuring some parts of the architecture. The overall color palette includes cream and blue for the building, teal green for the shutters, iron fence, and railings, and vibrant shades of red, pink, and purple for the foliage. The pavement and path are a pale, neutral color, while shadowed areas are rendered in cool blue tones.
title: Cast Iron Garden Balcony
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
